skill.name: freshservice-automation
skill.description: Automate Freshservice ITSM tasks via Rube MCP (Composio): create/update tickets, bulk operations, service requests, and outbound emails. Always search tools first for current schemas.
skill.summary: Manage Freshservice tickets, service requests, bulk updates, and outbound email through Rube MCP.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All 67 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code spans, documented identifiers, code fences, and the expected Rube MCP endpoint. Semantic review found three medium risks involving delegated access, bulk changes, and outbound email without explicit confirmation controls.

remediation.issue: The setup delegates Freshservice authentication and tool execution to a third-party MCP service.
remediation.suggestion: Verify the Rube endpoint, privacy terms, and requested scopes before authentication. Use a least-privilege Freshservice account.

remediation.issue: Bulk updates can change many tickets and may partially succeed without a required preview.
remediation.suggestion: Require a preview of ticket identifiers and changes, then obtain explicit user confirmation before running the bulk update.

remediation.issue: Outbound email can contact recipients and create new contacts without a required confirmation step.
remediation.suggestion: Show recipients, sender configuration, subject, and body before sending. Require explicit confirmation for external messages and new contacts.

static_findings.snippet: - Active Freshservice connection via `RUBE_MANAGE_CONNECTIONS` with toolkit `freshservice`
- Always call `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` first to get current tool schemas
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
1. Verify Rube MCP is available by confirming `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` responds
1. `FRESHSERVICE_LIST_TICKETS` - List tickets with optional filtering and pagination [Required]
2. `FRESHSERVICE_GET_TICKET` - Get detailed information for a specific ticket [Optional]
- `updated_since`: ISO 8601 timestamp to get tickets updated after this time
- Each `include` value consumes additional API credits
- `email`: Requester's email address (provide either email or requester_id)
- Either `email` or `requester_id` must be provided to identify the requester
- `ids`: Array of ticket IDs to update (required)
- `email_config_id`: Email configuration ID for the sender address
- `email_config_id` determines which email address the notification appears to come from
1. `FRESHSERVICE_CREATE_SERVICE_REQUEST` - Create a service request for a catalog item [Required]
- `item_display_id`: Display ID of the catalog item (required)
- `custom_fields`: Custom field values for the service item form
- `parent_ticket_id`: Display ID of a parent ticket (for child requests)
- `item_display_id` can be found in Admin > Service Catalog > item URL (e.g., /service_catalog/items
- Each `include` option consumes additional API credits
- Response data may be nested under `data` or `data.data`
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
- Ticket IDs can be the internal ID or the display_id shown in the UI
- `email_config_id`: Email configuration ID for the sender address

semantic_findings.title: Third-Party MCP Trust Boundary
semantic_findings.description: The setup delegates Freshservice authentication and tool execution to Rube MCP. Administrators must trust this service with ITSM access and ticket data.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The setup explicitly adds an external MCP endpoint and directs users through Freshservice authentication. Delegated access is necessary but creates a clear trust boundary.

semantic_findings.title: Bulk Changes Lack Mandatory Confirmation
semantic_findings.description: The workflow can update multiple tickets and may partially succeed. It does not require a preview or explicit confirmation before changing records.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented workflow performs bulk updates and warns about partial success. No preview or confirmation requirement appears in the workflow.

semantic_findings.title: Outbound Email Lacks Mandatory Confirmation
semantic_findings.description: The workflow can send email and create a contact for an unknown address. It does not require recipient verification or user confirmation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow explicitly sends outbound email and may create a contact. No confirmation step is included before these external side effects.

content.value_statement: Freshservice work becomes slow when tickets require repeated manual updates. This skill uses Rube MCP to search, create, update, and route ITSM records.
actual_capabilities: Lists Freshservice tickets with filters, sorting, pagination, and optional related data.
Retrieves detailed information for a specified ticket identifier.
Creates incident or service request tickets with requester and classification fields.
Applies the same field changes across multiple selected tickets.
Creates tickets while sending outbound email notifications.
Submits service catalog requests with quantities, custom fields, and optional parent tickets.
limitations: Requires an active Rube MCP connection and authenticated Freshservice access.
Tool schemas may change, so RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS must be called before each workflow.
Bulk updates apply identical fields to every selected ticket and may partially succeed.
Freshservice rate limits, API credits, permissions, and approval workflows still apply.

use_cases.title: Review an incident queue
use_cases.description: List recent high-priority tickets, paginate through results, and retrieve details for selected incidents.

use_cases.title: Standardize ticket updates
use_cases.description: Find a defined ticket set and apply one approved status, priority, group, or tag change.

use_cases.title: Submit catalog requests
use_cases.description: Create service requests for approved catalog items with requester details and required custom fields.

prompt_templates.title: List recent tickets
prompt_templates.prompt: List Freshservice tickets updated since [ISO date]. Sort by [field] in [direction] order and return [count] results per page.

prompt_templates.title: Create an incident
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Freshservice incident for [requester email]. Use subject [subject], description [description], status [status], and priority [priority]. Confirm before creation.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a bulk update
prompt_templates.prompt: Find tickets matching [criteria]. Preview their identifiers and current values, then ask before changing [fields] to [values].

prompt_templates.title: Create an outbound email ticket
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare an outbound email ticket for [recipient]. Show the sender configuration, subject, body, status, priority, and CC list before asking for confirmation.

output_examples.input: List open urgent tickets updated since 2026-07-01.
output_examples.output: Found 12 matching tickets. The first page shows each ticket identifier, subject, requester, status, priority, and last update time.
Prepared three updates from the current status to Pending. No changes were applied because confirmation is still required.

output_examples.input: Create a laptop service request for alex@example.com.
output_examples.output: The request needs a catalog item identifier and any required custom fields before it can be submitted.

best_practices: Search for current tool schemas before every workflow and validate required fields.
Preview identifiers, recipients, and changes before any write operation, then request explicit confirmation.
Paginate large queries, minimize optional includes, and handle rate limits with backoff.
anti_patterns: Do not update broad ticket sets without reviewing exact identifiers and proposed changes.
Do not send outbound email before verifying recipients, sender configuration, subject, and body.
Do not assume numeric status or priority codes match their text labels without validation.

faq.question: What connection does this skill require?
faq.answer: It requires Rube MCP and an active Freshservice connection created through the Freshservice toolkit.

faq.question: Can it search older tickets?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide an updated_since timestamp and paginate until the returned page contains fewer results than requested.

faq.question: Can each ticket receive different bulk changes?
faq.answer: No. One bulk call applies the same update fields to every selected ticket.

faq.question: Can it create a contact automatically?
faq.answer: Yes. Ticket creation may create a contact when the supplied email does not match an existing contact.

faq.question: Does it support service catalog requests?
faq.answer: Yes. It accepts a catalog item identifier, requester email, quantity, custom fields, and an optional parent ticket.

faq.question: How should partial bulk failures be handled?
faq.answer: Review every result, record successful updates, and retry only failed tickets after checking the reported errors.
